summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-surgical malabsorption and hypoglycemia requiring continuous gastrostomy tube feeds presented with recurrent sharp pain at the G-tube site after running out of oxycodone, without fever, chills, nausea/vomiting, or tube feed intolerance. Exam showed a clean, intact tube site without erythema or induration, and labs/urinalysis were unremarkable. She was admitted overnight to the bariatric surgery service for symptom control, maintained NPO by mouth with continuous tube feeds, monitored closely without evidence of infection or bleeding, and her pain was managed with oral oxycodone with brief IV hydromorphone for breakthrough before transitioning back to oral-only therapy. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, ambulatory, tolerating her tube feeding regimen, and was discharged home with instructions to resume home continuous feeds (NutriHep 50 cc/hr), monitor blood sugars, continue home medications, use PRN pain medications safely, and follow up with her surgeon.
